title: About
text:
I’m a geography graduate from the University of Galway specialising in GIS and spatial analysis. My dissertation measured 35 years of urban sprawl in Galway using CORINE land cover data, and I’ve built public-facing StoryMaps for Galway County Council.
I’m looking for graduate GIS roles in Ireland, the UK and Europe.

title: Rainfall interpolation by kriging
text:
QuestionHow can scattered rain gauge readings be turned into a reliable rainfall map, and where is that map least certain?
  ToolsR
  DataEDIT: rainfall station dataset and study area
  ContextGIS module assignment, University of Galway

title: Rainfall interpolation by kriging
text:
Problem
Rainfall is measured at a limited number of stations, but planning and environmental work need values everywhere. Kriging predicts values between stations and, unlike simpler methods, also gives an error estimate for each location.

title: Rainfall interpolation by kriging
text:
Data

Add: the station dataset, number of stations, time period and study area.

title: Rainfall interpolation by kriging
text:
Method

Explored the station data and checked for trend and outliers
Fitted an empirical variogram and a variogram model to describe how rainfall similarity changes with distance
Ran ordinary kriging over a prediction grid
Mapped both the predicted rainfall surface and the kriging variance
Checked accuracy with cross-validation

title: Rainfall interpolation by kriging
text:
Result



Predicted rainfall surface (left) and kriging variance (right).

title: Galway urban sprawl, 1990–2025
text:
QuestionHow far and in which direction has Galway's built-up area spread since 1990, and how did planning policy shape it?
  ToolsQGIS, R
  DataCORINE Land Cover (1990–2018 series and latest release), Galway City Development Plans
  CRSIrish Transverse Mercator (EPSG:2157)
  ContextBSc dissertation, University of Galway. Graded 78%.

title: Galway urban sprawl, 1990–2025
text:
Problem
Galway is one of the fastest-growing cities in Ireland. This project measured where that growth went between 1990 and 2025, and whether development followed the city plans or locked in a low-density pattern that later plans struggled to reverse (path dependency).

title: Galway urban sprawl, 1990–2025
text:
Data

CORINE Land Cover layers for each available year, reclassified to artificial surfaces vs. other cover
Galway City Development Plans, coded qualitatively for policy on density and expansion

title: Galway urban sprawl, 1990–2025
text:
Method

Reprojected all layers to ITM (EPSG:2157) so distances and areas are in metres
Calculated artificial-surface area per year and the change between periods
Built density gradients: share of built-up land in rings at set distances from the city centre
Tracked the centroid of built-up land each year to measure the direction and distance of shift
Coded development plan text for themes such as compact growth and suburban expansion, then compared policy timing with the spatial change

title: EV charger access, Galway City
text:
QuestionWhich neighbourhoods in Galway City are furthest by road from a public EV charger?
  ToolsQGIS
  DataCSO Census Small Areas, public EV charge point locations, OpenStreetMap road network
  CRSIrish Transverse Mercator (EPSG:2157)

title: EV charger access, Galway City
text:
Problem
Ireland’s EV targets depend on public charging, but straight-line distance hides how far people actually have to drive. This project measures road distance from each Census Small Area to its nearest charger to find the gaps.

title: EV charger access, Galway City
text:
Data

CSO Census Small Area boundaries, with population
Public EV charge point locations
OpenStreetMap road network, clipped to Galway City

title: EV charger access, Galway City
text:
Method

Converted Small Area polygons to centroids
Built a routable road network from OSM
Calculated the shortest road distance from each centroid to its nearest charger
Classified Small Areas into distance bands and mapped them as a choropleth

title: EV charger access, Galway City
text:
Result



Road distance to the nearest public EV charger by Census Small Area.



Add: your final map, plus 2–3 findings with numbers. For example: the share of Small Areas (or residents) more than 2 km by road from a charger, and which parts of the city are worst served.
